## Historical audit: S0300

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/historical_r1_C2_start/development/commons_187101683/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below are JSONL lines from this file; all observations are unsplit.

**Goal versus evidence:** The requested goal was a geometrically and visually faithful, editable reconstruction from one photograph, including camera and framing (line 1, H `model_request`). The student’s inventory interprets it as a living room with a sofa, coffee table, two tea settings, flowers, curtain and architecture. That interpretation is not independent verification of the reference image (line 3, H `model_response`).

| Stage | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Initial build | H emitted named assets with sofa cushions and arms, table legs, two cups and handles, plant stems and flowers, and architecture. It used colored primitives, a camera, world illumination and two area lights; no image textures are specified. Its comment claimed no fillet boxes, although the code uses them, so its approximately 130-primitive estimate is unreliable (lines 3–4). |
| First review and revision | The runner reported a successful build and render and selected step 1 (lines 6, 8–10). After the render and reference were supplied, H claimed the sofa was small and pale, the table too far left, camera too steep, curtain striped and plant sparse. It enlarged and recolored the sofa, shifted the table, lowered the camera and added folds and foliage; the revised code was executed (lines 11, 13–14). These are student diagnoses, not independently verified defects. |
| Second review and revision | Step 2 built and rendered successfully and was selected (lines 16, 18–20). H then claimed insufficient sofa height, visible table-leg ends, pale upholstery, regular curtain and sparse lower foliage. Step 3 extended sofa and legs downward, changed colors and lighting, and added foliage and folds; camera settings remained as in step 2 (lines 21, 23–24). |
| Final visible outcome | Step 3 built and rendered with return codes 0 and was selected (lines 26, 28–30). This establishes **execution success**, not visual or geometric correctness. No subsequent student review or formal quality verdict is visible. |

**Scene checks and uncertainty:** The programs specify multiple distinct objects and colored surfaces, but no procedural or image texture; labels such as upholstery and ceramic do not prove material fidelity. Named child parts and approximate coordinates show intended assembly, not verified physical connection or support. The pillow and curtain folds have explicit rotations; no articulated human pose is involved. Camera and lighting were adjusted, and renders completed without reported technical interruption, but the images themselves are not visible in this audit. Consequently, coverage, occlusions, part connections, color, texture, framing and whether either revision improved the match remain unresolved.

**Teacher and exploration:** No separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or student receipt of teacher feedback appears. The comparison instructions and images in runner requests were inputs, while the discrepancy claims and revisions were H’s own. H performed two render-driven revisions; the recorded sessions show no autonomous tool calls (lines 2, 12, 22). The initial primitive-count contradiction illustrates a transferable need to check expanded helper costs against code. The specific sofa, curtain and foliage adjustments remain task-specific hypotheses, not validated lessons.
